title: Jordan’s 2026, wrapped
label: Jordan’s 2026 on Claude, a recap you tap through

slides.headline: Jordan, here’s your 2026 on Claude.
body: Eleven months, a lot of open tabs.

slides.headline: New year, new lesson plans.
items: Rebuilt your eighth-grade water cycle unit around a hands-on lab
Wrote a grading rubric your students could actually read
Named your sourdough starter Gerald

slides.headline: The spreadsheet month.
items: Built a gradebook template that color-codes late work
Drafted the science fair parent letter in English and Spanish
Planned a sign-out system for the classroom library

slides.headline: Science fair, survived.
items: Coached 23 projects from “I have no idea” to poster board
Wrote the judges’ score sheets
Started Python for Everybody, one evening at a time

slides.headline: April and May: off the record.
body: Nothing from these two made it into my notes. Testing season, probably. We’ll call it a quiet stretch.

slides.headline: Summer school, but for you.
items: Finished Python for Everybody
Wrote your first real script: it renamed 300 class photos in four seconds
Mapped out a road trip through Utah’s national parks

slides.headline: Builder mode.
items: Started Lab Notes, a web app for logging classroom experiments
Learned enough Git to stop being scared of it
Finished the first course of a UX design certificate

slides.headline: Back-to-school speedrun.
items: Rewrote your syllabus to fit on one page
Rolled Lab Notes out to three classes as a beta
Pitched a coding club to your principal. They said yes.

slides.headline: Coding club is live.
items: Fourteen students at the first meeting
Wrote six weekly challenges, starting with a number-guessing game
Sent off a talk proposal to the state science teachers’ conference

slides.headline: Your most-played month.
items: Talk proposal accepted
Wrote and rehearsed the 20-minute version, then the 15-minute version
Shipped Lab Notes v2 with photo uploads
Finished a second Python course on data structures

slides.headline: And you’re still going.
items: Conference talk coming up on November 14
Drafting a grant application for classroom laptops

slides.headline: All year, on repeat.
items: Sunday lesson-plan check-ins
Gerald the sourdough starter, somehow still alive

slides.headline: Your top genres.
items: Lesson planning
Learning Python
Building Lab Notes
Coding club
Event wrangling

slides.headline: Your 2026 personality: the Teacher Who Ships.
slides.lead: Lesson planner. Python learner. App builder. Club founder.
body: You learn something on Monday and teach it by Friday.

slides.headline: One honest note.
body: You started four big things this year and finished three. The UX certificate stalled after course one.
Pick it back up in January, or let it go on purpose. Either is fine.

slides.headline: That’s a wrap, Jordan.
body: Here’s to 2027. Go give that talk.
